`path-preview.json` contains full, unrounded [x, y, heading, active segment]
traces generated by calling `simulatePathWithTrace` in an untouched checkout of
BLine-Web at the commit recorded in the file, using its default limits.
The inputs were constructed as native BLine waypoint/rotation/event models
independently of Mayhem's adapter. Each case begins with its explicit start
waypoint; target waypoints use a 0.45 m radius. These golden samples test both
the model adapter and runtime/playback integration, including handoff ticks,
against the external implementation rather than against Mayhem itself.

`path-constraints.json` records the untouched upstream joint constraint
generator's speed caps and radii for a three-leg route with and without manual
pins. The native inputs were authored independently of Mayhem's adapter, using
the same defaults and robot dimensions. Adapter tests compare the full output
values and solve status against those external results.

`robot-machines.json` holds real state machines from the 3256 offseason robot's
`robot.mayhem.json`: `oldShotCycle` (commit ba22adc, unnamed transitions whose labels
overlapped in the old graph layout) and `current` (Superstructure, a fully connected priority
supervisor; IntakeSequence; ShotCycle). `e2e/state-graph-layout.spec.ts` checks that their
edge labels never overlap each other or a state and stay inside the graph. `latest` is the
same file later (Superstructure as explicit button edges plus a few `"*"` rows, long input
names); the spec checks that no condition chip runs past its card in a narrow inspector, and that
the Superstructure graph fits a laptop window readably.

`robot-project.json` is the whole 3256 offseason `robot.mayhem.json` (five pose-chain autos of
20 to 46 steps, and the three machines). `e2e/auto-paths.spec.ts` checks that each auto's graph
collapses pass-through points into "Drive path" cards and fits a laptop window without scrolling.
